gaps.sentence: Unless it ___ below five degrees tonight, the event will go ahead.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' clauses take the present simple even when referring to tonight: drops.

gaps.sentence: She wishes she ___ the job offer when it came.
gaps.explanation: Regret about a past decision takes the past perfect: had accepted.

gaps.sentence: I will be surprised if he ___ on time for once.
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a real future condition takes the present simple: arrives.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ so much cake — I feel sick now.
gaps.hint: past act with a present consequence
gaps.explanation: The regret is about a past action, so 'wish' takes the past perfect: had not eaten.

gaps.sentence: If plants ___ enough light, their leaves turn yellow.
gaps.hint: a general truth in the if-clause
gaps.explanation: Zero conditionals state general truths with the present simple in both clauses: do not get.

gaps.sentence: Should you ___ any problems, please contact support.
gaps.explanation: 'Should you plus infinitive' is a formal way to say 'If you ...': experience.

gaps.sentence: If you had set an alarm, you ___.
gaps.explanation: The present result of a past unreal condition takes 'would not be': would not still be asleep.

gaps.sentence: He would be healthier if he ___ so much red meat.
gaps.hint: an unreal present habit, past simple
gaps.explanation: For an unreal present habit, the if-clause uses the past simple: did not eat.
